Synopsis:
Two gith kids are pushing a chest (which secretly contains a gremishka) back and forth between them using their Mage Hands. You can tell them to stop and if you insist, eventually they'll step back from the box, letting the gremishka break out. Alternatively, if you try to join in or fail to get them to stop, they'll start shoving you.

Cluster Contexts:
- CRE_General_MageHandMain.json: You’ve come upon two gith children in the creche/monastery area tossing a locked chest back and forth with Mage Hand; the box actually hides a gremishka that will burst free if the kids are made to step away. The children are skittish and insultingly dismissive of interruptions (their “k’chakhi” insult), so a polite admonition can make them retreat and release the creature, while trying to join their game or failing to stop them can provoke them into shoving you. This scene sits near the Vlaakith portrait and other githyanki trappings, so nearby NPCs (notably Lae’zel or a gith avatar, if present) will react in race-specific ways and a prior attempt to vandalize the portrait may already be noticed by the youth. Giths here are generally distrustful and quick to defend their space, so expect sharp, defensive responses.
- CRE_MageHandKid01.json: One of the gith kids can't wait for the player to open the chest (knowing that a gremishka will pop out.) Before opening chest - gleeful anticipation. After opening chest - laughing in the player's face. If chest stolen - sulky.
- CRE_MageHandKid02.json: One of the gith kids can't wait for the player to open the chest (knowing that a gremishka will pop out.) Before opening chest - gleeful anticipation. After opening chest - laughing in the player's face.
- CRE_General_AD_MageHandKidLaughingAtPlayer.json: Gith kid comments about the gremishka coming out of the chest.
- CRE_General_VlaakithPortrait.json: You're in the gith crèche before a grand portrait of Queen Vlaakith; Lae'zel stands nearby, reverent toward Vlaakith and openly hostile to any mention of Orpheus. Off-screen you have already met the gith youth (Varrl) and know he’s been secretly reading outlawed writings about Orpheus. Depending on prior choices Varrl may be unharmed and persuadable (able to hand over part of chapter 2), or he may be injured from an earlier fight in which case you can either steal the chapter or heal him before continuing. The player can attempt to vandalize the portrait (for example by drawing a new face) and the nearby Varrl may catch you—he admires Orpheus, fears reprisals for speaking his name, and will respond with gratitude if you show him compassion.

context: You’ve walked into a gith crèche where two gith children are using Mage Hand to toss a locked chest back and forth; the box actually conceals a gremishka that will burst out if the children are made to step away. The kids are skittish and insultingly dismissive of interruptions—one spits the k'chakhi insult ("idiot")—and they react differently depending on how you approach: a firm, polite admonition can make them back off and free the creature, while trying to join their game or failing to stop them can provoke them to shove you. The youth are gleeful at the thought of the gremishka and will laugh if it pops out; if you try to steal the box they grow sulky. This scene sits before a grand Vlaakith portrait (Lae’zel or a gith avatar may be nearby and react to your behavior), and a previously met youth (Varrl) or prior actions around the portrait can influence nearby responses.
